summary_responses.subtopic: Federal Credit Union Chartering & Associational Common Bond Rules
summary_responses.response: The National Credit Union Administration Board issued a final rule (12 CFR Part 701, RIN 3133-AF93) amending its Chartering and Field of Membership Manual to revise criteria for associational common bonds, effective January 4, 2027. The rule clarifies that requiring members to purchase a good, product, or service as a condition of membership will no longer automatically disqualify a group from being recognized as an association. It retains the long-standing policy that associations based primarily on a client-customer relationship do not meet associational common bond requirements, but replaces the automatic bar — previously illustrated by the fraternal association insurance example — with a totality-of-the-circumstances test to determine if the relationship is merely incidental. Finalized with modifications to the April 8, 2026 proposal after considering 18 public comments, the rule adds transparency by detailing review criteria, providing relevant examples, and simplifying the review process for pre-approved groups. The amendments apply only to single associational and multiple common bond federal credit unions and do not affect occupational, community, or federally insured state-chartered credit unions.

summary_responses.subtopic: Federal Reserve Regulation D & Depository Institution Reserve Requirements
summary_responses.response: The Federal Reserve Board issued a final rule amending Regulation D to annually index the reserve requirement exemption amount and low reserve tranche for 2027, effective December 18, 2026 and applicable beginning January 1, 2027. The reserve requirement exemption amount will remain unchanged at $39.2 million from 2026 because total reservable liabilities of all depository institutions decreased 2.4 percent from $21.103 trillion to $20.588 trillion between June 30, 2025 and June 30, 2026, and the Federal Reserve Act provides for no downward adjustment. The low reserve tranche will increase to $688.5 million from $674.1 million in 2026, reflecting a statutory formula of 80 percent of the 2.7 percent increase in net transaction accounts from $17.012 trillion to $17.465 trillion over the same period. The Board noted that this annual indexation is required by Section 19(b) of the Federal Reserve Act even though it set all reserve requirement ratios to zero percent in March 2020. Consequently the 2027 adjustments are ministerial and will have no practical effect on depository institutions, whose reserve requirements will remain zero.

It would also introduce an enhanced rebate of $0.0038 per share for adding displayed liquidity in TXSE-listed corporate securities priced at or above $1.00 to incentivize quoting and deepen liquidity. Additionally, the Exchange proposes to revise its Lead Market Maker Program by redefining "Size Near the Inside" to require minimum notional value on both sides within 0.25% of the NBBO for at least 95% of the trading day and "Time at NBBO" to average time spent at the NBB and NBO separately, plus adding notes to exclude periods when the SIP NBBO is missing, locked or crossed and to adjust percentage thresholds for leveraged ETPs. TXSE states the changes, proposed to be effective November 2, 2026, are for business and competitive reasons to encourage displayed liquidity and are consistent with Sections 6(b)(4) and 6(b)(5) of the Exchange Act for equitable allocation of reasonable fees and just and equitable principles of trade.

summary_responses.response: The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services announced in notice CMS-8092-N the Medicare Part A inpatient hospital deductible and related coinsurance amounts for calendar year 2027, effective January 1, 2027, as required by Section 1813 of the Social Security Act. CMS waived notice-and-comment rulemaking for the announcement, stating the amounts are determined by statutory formula and do not establish a new substantive legal standard.

While some current regulations list only paper methods and others allow both paper and electronic options, the FAA already requests payment via the Treasury's Pay gov portal, and the rule would standardize the regulations with that practice, allowing alternative methods only where otherwise authorized by law and updating related guidance forms. The FAA estimates the change would save the agency 99815 dollars annually — about 457125 dollars over five years at a 3 percent discount rate and 1 point 4 million dollars in perpetuity — with de minimis transition costs for customers, and it is accepting public comments through January 4, 2027 via the federal eRulemaking portal, mail, hand delivery or fax.

summary_responses.subtopic: National Park Administration, Conservation & Multi-Use Trail Regulation
summary_responses.response: The National Park Service has issued a final rule effective December 21, 2026, amending special regulations for Mammoth Cave National Park in Kentucky under 36 CFR Part 7. The rule allows the park superintendent to designate approximately 37 miles of multi-use trails for bicycle use, including electric bicycles where authorized, and permits horseback riding on the 5.4-mile Houchin Ferry North/Ollie Road. The action implements the selected alternative from the park's 2024 Comprehensive Land and River Trails Plan and Environmental Assessment and the December 2024 Finding of No Significant Impact, which was developed to replace outdated plans and address deteriorating trail conditions. Under the plan, bicycle use will be discontinued on the White Oak Trail and the Maple Springs Connector Trail, which will be closed and restored, while the Mammoth Cave Railroad Bike and Hike Trail will remain open and eight new trails will be constructed to create the expanded network. The NPS determined the changes will improve trail sustainability and drainage, expand high-quality recreation for hikers, bikers, equestrians and paddlers, and protect natural and cultural resources, with designated trails to be publicized through the Superintendent's Compendium and park maps.
